newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate eases to 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate eases to 10.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate eased 10 basis points to 10.3 percent on Thursday amid high banking sector liquidity, dealers said.

They said daily supply of kuna funds rose to 110 million, against less than half that in demand. Of 53.7 million kuna settlements, some 36 million were new borrowings by banks beefing up for the long week-end with Friday's public holiday.
The call money rate jumped to 10 from 8.3 percent after two deals were struck at 12 and 16 percent, up from nine.
Other rates ranged from a steady 8.0 percent for insurers' one-week funds to 15 percent on two-month interbank loans.
Wednesday's overnight trade totalled 10.3 million kuna as one bank borrowed money for reserve payment.
The central bank's kuna midrates valid until Monday firmed slightly to 5.3847 against the dollar and 3.5632 to the mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
